root.name: Philidor Defense: Hanham, Kmoch Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 Nd7 4. Bc4 c6 5. Ng5

overview: In the Hanham with ...Nd7 and ...c6 White plays 5.Ng5, threatening Nxf7 and aiming at the weak f7 square. Black usually replies 5...Nh6 and 6.f4 Be7 with ...O-O and a solid centre with ...d5. White holds a lead in space, Black a compact camp and counter blows with ...exd4 or ...d5.

white_ideas.idea: Hit f7 with Ng5 and Bc4
Support the centre with f4 and c3
Castle and push e5 or dxe5

black_ideas.idea: Castle and keep a compact position

typical_structures.structure: Philidor pawns on d6 and e5 against White e4 and d4

character.notes: Black is compact and a little passive; White presses with a tricky f7 target.

gambit.notes: No material is given up in the main line.

structure.notes: The e5-d6 and e4-d4 tension can resolve either way.

approach.notes: Less usual than main Philidor lines but a known set-up.

level.notes: Needs some theory on f7 traps and a feel for when to play ...d5.

sublines_that_differ.name: Berger Variation
sublines_that_differ.moves: 5. Ng5 Nh6 6. f4 Be7 7. O-O O-O 8. c3 d5
sublines_that_differ.how: Black gets ...d5 in with a good game.

character.reason: Black is compact but White pressure on f7 gives some bite, and neither is clearly the main theme.

gambit.reason: No pawn is given up in the main line.

soundness.reason: Nothing is refuted for either side.

structure.reason: The e4-d4 centre is in tension with Black e5-d6.

approach.reason: A known line in the Philidor.

level.reason: Moderate theory and understanding of the tension in the centre.

plans.reason: White aims at f7 and holds more space.
